title: Updated report of COVID-19 vaccine safety monitoring in Japan: booster doses for Omicron variants and vaccinations for infants and young children.
ehr_evidence: individual case safety reports from healthcare professionals and the marketing authorisation holder (MAH)
summary: Updated report of COVID-19 vaccine safety monitoring in Japan covering booster doses for Omicron variants and vaccinations for infants and young children until March 2023.
key_findings: 39 confirmed cases of myocarditis and 18 of pericarditis for any Pfizer booster doses.
24 confirmed cases of myocarditis and 13 of pericarditis for any Moderna booster doses.
Only 1 death was confirmed as causally related to vaccination (42-year-old woman, Pfizer BA.4/BA.5).
Reporting rates of serious adverse events for bivalent Omicron vaccines were generally not higher than for any booster doses.
Reporting rate of serious adverse events was low in children aged 6 months to 4 years.
captured_features: adverse event types (myocarditis, pericarditis, anaphylaxis, death)
population: individuals aged ≥12 years and infants/young children aged 6 months to 4 years in Japan
exposure_domain: COVID-19 vaccination (booster doses for Omicron variants)
limitations: underestimation of the numbers and incidence rates of adverse events by using the spontaneous reporting data
data_availability_statement: The data for this report are available to the public (Japanese language only) in the webpage of the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare of Japan ( https://www.mhlw.go.jp/stf /shingi/shingi-kousei_284075. html).
